history.summary: A Kalyanji (Vishnu) temple in Tonk town itself, distinct from the two better-known Kalyanji shrines of the district: seq 2113, the NMA-protected 'Kalyanraiji's Temple' at Todaraisingh (~48 km away), and the famous Diggi Kalyanji at Diggi, Malpura tehsil (~60 km away, rebuilt 1527 CE under Rana Sanga). Evidence for the Tonk-town shrine is thin: an Instagram place listing 'Kalyan Ji Ka Mandir, Tonk, RJ' (pin 26.156782, 75.783191, near Tonk 304001); it also appears as a Tonk-town attraction on some travel sites, though those may be conflating it with Diggi. FLAG - identity is provisional: no published history, timings or description found for this specific temple; verify locally whether it is a modest neighbourhood shrine. Not to be confused with the 19th-century 'Shree Kalyan Rai jee ka Mandir' at Kakor (IGNCA RJ/TNK-085, ~20 km from Tonk; Kakor is separately covered by CSV row 893 'Kakor Fort and Temple'). Coordinates are a Tonk-town approximation.

name: Kalyanji Temple, Tonk
town_description: Tonk is a historic city in south-eastern Rajasthan on the right bank of the Banas River, about 95 km south of Jaipur. It was the capital of the only Muslim-ruled princely state in Rajasthan (the Nawabs of Tonk, 1817-1947), and is known for the Jama Masjid, Sunahari Kothi, Arabic and Persian Research Institute, Hathi Bhata rock carvings, and a cluster of old temples including Jal Devi Mandir and Mahadevali Shiv Mandir.

travel.railway: Tonk has no railway station; nearest major railheads Jaipur (~95 km) and Sawai Madhopur (~85 km, verify)
travel.road: On NH-52 (Jaipur-Kota road); well connected by bus and taxi from Jaipur
